Thanks Karthik / Marissa — attaching the sample request traces and a top-level traffic expectation for Q4. High level: 30k daily active users, expected 2.6 requests per user/day, median request = 850 tokens in, 2200 tokens generated. Peak concurrency window is 09:00–11:00 PT with a 3x amplification over baseline.

We need a committed monthly TPS target for our procurement team by Friday so we can lock in budget. Can you run an initial tokens/sec estimate + headroom guidance? Also flag any latency SLO gaps if we commit to the 99th percentile < 350ms for generation.

Attachments: nimbus_workload_samples.csv (csv)

—Evan

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com; monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing inputs + sample workload

Evan — thanks for the traces, that helps. Quick read and first-pass numbers below (I'll follow up with a heatmap graphic and sensitivity table by tomorrow):

Summary first-pass (ballpark):
- Baseline expected tokens/sec served (avg across day): ~4200 tokens/sec
- Peak tokens/sec (09:00–11:00): ~12,600 tokens/sec (3x baseline)
- Aggressive headroom for 2x peak: plan for 25k tokens/sec to tolerate traffic bursts and model warm-up variability

Latency SLO fit (99th percentile < 350ms):
- With single-precision model and 16-GPU slab (A100-equivalent, optimized kernels), we estimate p99 generation latency ~280–320ms at peak with continuous batching tuned to 50ms window.
- If you insist on a tighter 250ms p99, we will likely need dedicated 24 GPU equivalent at the peak slab or lower batch windows which increases cost ~18–25%.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll attach a capacity heatmap showing tokens/sec vs GPU slabs (tomorrow).
2) Marissa / Monica will propose a mutually acceptable committed TPS and a fallback burst plan to satisfy procurement.
3) If procurement needs a concrete cost delta for 250ms vs 350ms, we'll run a quick cost-per-token delta.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Evan Cook <evan.cook@nimbus-systems.com>

Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -07:00

Evan — looping in Monica who will own the procurement convo and propose committed tiers.

Monica, is the following commitment profile something Nimbus could consider?
- Commit tier A: 10k tokens/sec reserved (monthly) — covers baseline + small bursts; p99 target 350ms; 12 month term.
- Commit tier B: 20k tokens/sec reserved — covers expected peak with 1.25x safety; p99 350ms; priority capacity with short-failover to shared pool.
- Burst addon: 10k tokens/sec burst pool billed per-token for occasional spikes.

If they push for p99=250ms we would recommend Tier C (24k+) reserved slab and a staged rollout (can share cost estimates).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement wants concrete numbers and a short SLA note. Two quick clarifications before we sign: 1) what does the 25k tokens/sec "aggressive headroom" translate to in GPU count and monthly committed spend? 2) if we accept Tier B (+burst), what fallback behavior can we expect if the dedicated slab is saturated?

We aim to decide by EOD Friday.

—Evan
From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: Evan Cook <evan.cook@nimbus-systems.com>; procurement@nimbus-systems.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com; marissa_cole@redwood.com; sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing inputs + sample workload

Evan / Procurement team — answers below and quick attachments (sizing-heatmap-v1.png and mutual-action-plan-v2.docx):

1) 25k tokens/sec aggressive headroom -> approximately 18 A100-equivalent GPUs in a warm dedicated pool (continuous batching, 50ms batching latency). Estimated committed monthly price (list, before discounts): $128,500/month. We can provide exact pricing depending on contract length and burst policies.

2) Fallback behavior for Tier B (20k reserved + 10k burst):
- Primary: traffic served from reserved slab (20k tokens/sec).
- Secondary: burst pool (best-effort, per-token billing) up to requested burst capacity depending on spare cluster headroom; bursts are not SLA-backed but typically maintain similar latencies when spare capacity exists.
- Degradation policy: if both reserved and burst pools are saturated, we enable graceful degradation: short-circuiting longer generations (configurable max tokens), model variant fallback (quantized variant) and explicit 429 rate signals to client. We will document expected p99 impact for worst-case saturation scenarios.

Action items:
- Evan: Confirm whether Nimbus wants pricing with a 12- or 24-month commitment (we'll refine discounts).
- Procurement: we'll produce an SLA note and an isolation diagram for your security review by Monday EOD.

Attachments: sizing-heatmap-v1.png (image), mutual-action-plan-v2.docx (docx)

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
